evidence: The target contains two disconnected black components, each with one left port and one right port.
Both guides use S-bends to bring the cores into a long close, parallel central section, then fan back out to separated output ports.
There is no closed interferometer loop, splitter tree, grating, or resonator; the function is set by evanescent coupling in the long central overlap.
topology_reasoning.working_principle: Power transfer is governed primarily by the even/odd supermode phase accumulated over the close parallel section. The S-bends provide adiabatic access from widely separated ports into the small coupling gap.
function_defining_knobs: coupling_length: length of the close parallel interaction region
coupling_gap: edge-to-edge spacing between the two cores in the central section
s_bend_xspan: horizontal run used by the access S-bends
port_y_offset: input/output port separation from the center
coupler_center_offset: half separation of the coupled guide centerlines
bend_radius: smoothing radius for the access bends
topology_reasoning.modeling_plan: Use two gf.Path centerlines through measured port, bend, and coupler centers, smooth with Euler bends, and extrude on layer (1,0). Keep all tunables as top-level assignments. Record real path lengths in lengths.json.

iterations.change_made: Initial two smoothed S-bend paths with constant guide width and close central coupling section.
Changed access sections to direct Manhattan-style path controls with corrected port separation; central section remained path-extruded.
Replaced low-fidelity constant-width path body with calibrated primitives-only rectangle silhouette; retained top-level coupler tunables and path-derived lengths for knob response.
